headlines.title: Texas Instruments board declares fourth quarter 2026 quarterly dividend
headlines.summary: The board of directors of Texas Instruments Incorporated (Nasdaq: TXN) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.52 per share of common stock, payable Nov. 10, 2026, to stockholders of record on Oct. 30, 2026.

headlines.title: TXN to Report Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell the Stock?
headlines.summary: Texas Instruments gears up for Q3 earnings, with strong analog and embedded chip demand fueling growth, while geopolitical tensions pose risks.

headlines.title: What Does Texas Instruments (TXN) New AI Data Center Launch Mean For Investors?
headlines.summary: Texas Instruments (NasdaqGS:TXN) announced new high-performance analog to digital converters and power management chips for AI data centers on 14 October 2026. The product family targets hyperscale operators that are seeking tighter control of power delivery, signal integrity and thermal monitoring across AI servers. TI is positioning these components to address downtime risks and reliability constraints as AI workloads raise data center energy and density demands.

headlines.title: Texas Instruments (TXN) Stock Could Be 20% Overvalued As AI Data Center Push Grows
headlines.summary: Texas Instruments has more than doubled shareholders' money over the past three years, which puts a sharp spotlight on a simple question for you as an investor. Is the current share price still in line with the cash the business is expected to generate, or has sentiment moved ahead of the underlying stream of dollars? The stock has returned 103.3% over the past three years, so a lot of future cash flow is now effectively being priced in.

headlines.title: A Silent Winner: Texas Instruments Anchors the AI Supercycle
headlines.summary: Texas Instruments launched new power management and telemetry chips for AI data centers, positioning its analog business as a dividend-paying infrastructure play ahead of Q3 earnings on Oct. 21.

description: Texas Instruments Incorporated designs, manufactures, and sells semiconductors to electronics designers and manufacturers in the United States, China, the rest of Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Japan, and internationally. It operates through Analog and Embedded Processing segments. The Analog segment offers power products to manage power requirements across various voltage levels, including battery-management solutions, DC/DC switching regulators, AC/DC and isolated controllers and converters, power switches, linear regulators, voltage references, multiphase controllers and power stages, and lighting products. This segment also provides signal chain products that sense, condition, and measure real-world signals and convert them into data to be transferred or converted for further processing and control, such as amplifiers, data converters, interface products, motor drives, clocks, and logic and sensing products. The Embedded Processing segment offers microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity, and radar products; and applications processors for specific computing activity. It also provides DLP products primarily for use in projecting high-definition images; calculators; and application-specific integrated circuits. Its products are used in various markets, such as industrial, automotive, personal electronics, communications equipment, enterprise systems, calculators, and others. The company markets and sells its semiconductor products through direct sales and distributors, as well as through its website. Texas Instruments Incorporated was founded in 1930 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas.
